scope: Canonical path, source-root and target aliases, symlink containment, isolated-worktree roots, exact source staging, PATH-003 closure, prewrite behavior, and bounded path check/use races in the source stager and canonical prompt builder.

findings.title: The stager can write through a final target symlink installed after its prewrite check
findings.claim: Write mode checks target.is_symlink() and target type by pathname, then calls shutil.copy2 with the same pathname. Replacing the absent final target with a symlink after line 128 but before copy2 makes the copy follow that symlink and overwrite an external referent.

reproduction.swapBoundary: Inside the instrumented shutil.copy2 call, after all production prewrite checks and before the real copy2 opens the destination.

findings.impact: A concurrent actor able to change the worktree path can redirect a supposedly contained staged write outside the isolated worktree.
findings.remediation: Open and write the destination relative to verified directory descriptors with no-follow semantics, and atomically replace within the verified directory; do not separate the final-component check from the open/write operation.

findings.title: The stager can escape through an intermediate target directory swapped after containment checks
findings.claim: target_path checks each target component and returns a pathname. The source hash and other work occur before mkdir/copy2 use that pathname. Replacing a checked target directory with a symlink during that interval redirects the staged copy outside ROOT.

reproduction.swapBoundary: After target_path completed, during the subsequent source hash, before target.parent.mkdir and copy2.

findings.impact: A concurrent directory swap defeats target containment even though every component passed the earlier symlink walk.
findings.remediation: Walk from a trusted worktree directory descriptor with O_DIRECTORY/O_NOFOLLOW and perform creation and replacement relative to pinned descriptors.

findings.title: The stager accepts a source file replaced by a symlink after the source-tree scan
findings.claim: require_regular_tree rejects symlinks while collecting Path objects, but later hashing and copying reopen each pathname. Replacing a collected regular source file with a symlink before sha256 makes both hashing and copying consume the external referent, so post-copy hash verification still succeeds.

reproduction.swapBoundary: At the first production sha256 call for the already-scanned source file.

findings.impact: A concurrently mutable source tree can inject bytes from outside the approved source trees while the stager reports success.
findings.remediation: Pin source directories/files with no-follow descriptors, verify regular-file metadata on the opened descriptors, and hash/copy from the same opened file description.

findings.title: The prompt builder can overwrite an external file through a post-check output symlink
findings.claim: canonical_output_path validates output components and returns a pathname. Prompt construction then creates a broad interval before output.write_bytes reopens that pathname. Installing a final symlink in the interval makes write_bytes follow it.

reproduction.swapBoundary: After canonical_output_path returned and while canonical_prompt_bytes was instrumented, before output.write_bytes.

findings.impact: A concurrent actor can redirect canonical prompt output outside correctness-audit/packets/prompts and overwrite an external file.
findings.remediation: Create the output through pinned no-follow directory descriptors and atomically replace a verified in-directory target; never write through the checked pathname directly.

findings.title: A packet swap after source-only validation bypasses prompt content isolation
findings.claim: The builder canonicalizes and source-only-validates the packet by pathname, then reopens that pathname for header hashing and framing. Replacing the validated packet with a symlink to an external JSON document after validation causes unvalidated forbidden downstream content to enter the emitted prompt.

reproduction.swapBoundary: Immediately after validate_source_only_json returned, before header hashing and framed_section reads.

findings.impact: Concurrent mutation can bypass the source-only boundary and expose forbidden downstream information to a completeness or blind reviewer while the builder reports success.
findings.remediation: Open each approved input once with no-follow semantics, validate and render from the same immutable byte buffer (or pinned descriptor), and derive all recorded hashes from those exact bytes.

candidate4Path003Closure.qualification: PATH-004 is a distinct post-check replacement race; it does not negate the verified static PATH-003 fix.

sourceStaging.exclusionRule: __pycache__ directories and .pyc/.pyo files are excluded by the candidate stager

commands.evidence: All static, race, inventory, worktree, exact-head, and clean-status assertions passed
Independent nonblocking acquisition failed while the bounded holder was active

nonEvidenceAttempts.description: An initial stager --check and initial aggregate probe ran before the permitted ignored source trees were staged.
nonEvidenceAttempts.reasonExcluded: They exited 1 on the first missing staged file and are not used as evidence. The source trees were then staged under the continuously held lock, after which both checks passed.

conclusion: Candidate 5 preserves candidate 4's static PATH-003 closure and passes canonical alias, static symlink, worktree-root, and exact 1,098-file staging checks. It fails the specialty because five bounded post-check replacements reproducibly defeat target containment, source provenance, prompt output containment, or source-only prompt isolation.
